critic.verdict: The pull-back clearly serves the story: it opens tight on the man from behind and the freeway, then travels left and out to reveal the motel room, California map, lamp, bed and stacked circuit-board boxes that define his stake, ending on the complete plate which is a strong picture to dwell on. The man and boxes stay coherent through all six frames with no tearing, doubled edges, halo or ghost, nothing clips awkwardly, the halftone-shimmer suits the 1970s silkscreen print style, and the move reverses cleanly. The plate independently is clean: no stray text, the man is correctly seen from behind, no anachronism or mangled anatomy.

rounds.verdict: A coherent but timid, damped pull-back that does not deliver its intended reveal and lets one box drift against its stack — no better than a plain push-in.
filmIssues: The intended tight-on-the-boxes pull-back is heavily damped and barely reads: all six frames show almost the same full room, with only a slight shrink and drift right, so it is no more expressive than a plain centred move.

The opening frame is not the promised close view of the circuit-board boxes and the closing frame is not a decisive discovery of the man — the reveal of man-at-window after failure never actually happens.

cut-2 contains only part of the stacked boxes but is given depth 0.9, so that one box slides against the rest of the stack, bed and lamp that stay on the background; boxes that belong together do not stay together and a faint offset/doubling is visible in the stack.
The man has no purposeful settle or drift to give the contemplative moment weight, and halftone-shimmer is not perceptible in the frames.

plan.rationale: A quiet turning point after failure: the camera reveals tight on the circuit-board box, then travels out and right across the motel room to discover the man alone at the freeway window, his slow settle giving the moment weight.

rounds.verdict: A sound pull-back concept, but not publishable as rendered: the protagonist's late settle and the partially separated box stack undermine coherence, and the reveal is too timid to earn a high score.
filmIssues: The pull-back idea is right, but the man's 'settle' entrance at t=0.55 makes the protagonist shift/settle mid-film rather than being present and coherent from the opening; it reads as a late correction, not as part of the reveal.

cut-2 contains only the upper box of the stacked circuit-board boxes, while the rest of the stack stays in the clean background. With a different depth from the background it can pull away from the boxes below it, so a stack that belongs together does not stay convincingly glued together during the pull-back.

The executed move is only modest between t=0 and t=1: the opening is not decisively tight on the man and freeway, and the final reveal of the map, lamp, bed and full box stack is not much wider, so it is little better than a plain centred push-in/pull-out in storytelling force.
Because the move is playable in reverse, the late settle on the man is especially awkward on the return play, where it becomes an unexplained lift just before the tight opening frame.

plan.rationale: Reverse the timid move into a clear story pull-back: open tight on the man from behind at the glowing freeway window, then pull back and travel left to reveal the whole motel room — map, lamp, bed and the stacked circuit-board boxes that are his stake — ending on the full wide plate to dwell on. Lower, closer depths for both cut-outs keep the box stack glued to the room and the man free of ghostin
